questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: leading coefficient and width of a parabola
questions.learningObjective: compare the widths of two parabolas using the absolute value of the leading coefficient
questions.stem: An engineer overlays two trough models, y = 2x^2 and y = 0.5x^2, on the same set of axes and must state which trough is narrower.

options.text: The y = 2x^2 trough is narrower because the absolute value 2 is larger
The two troughs have identical widths because both have the form y = ax^2
options.misconception: ignores the role of the absolute value of the coefficient

options.text: The y = 0.5x^2 trough is narrower because 0.5 is less than 2
options.misconception: treats a smaller coefficient as producing a narrower opening

options.text: The widths cannot be compared without also knowing the constant k
options.misconception: believes the vertical shift changes the width of a parabola

questions.explanation: Width is governed by |a|, not by the sign or by any vertical shift. Since |2| is greater than |0.5|, the y = 2x^2 model grows faster away from the x-axis and traces the narrower trough; the flatter one belongs to y = 0.5x^2.
questions.hint: Compare the absolute values of the two leading coefficients.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: leading coefficient and width of a parabola
questions.learningObjective: solve for the leading coefficient from a measured point on a parabola
questions.stem: A suspension bridge cable is modeled by y = ax^2, and a surveyor measures that the cable hangs 4.5 units below the roadway when x is 3 units from the lowest point. Find the value of a.
questions.explanation: Substituting x = 3 and y = 4.5 into y = ax^2 gives 4.5 = 9a, so a = 0.5. Because |a| is less than 1, the cable falls away slowly, which is exactly the shape a long suspension span needs.
questions.hint: Divide the measured depth by the square of the horizontal distance.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: leading coefficient and width of a parabola
questions.learningObjective: explain why the sign of the leading coefficient does not affect width
questions.stem: A student argues that y = -6x^2 must be wider than y = x^2 because the negative sign stretches the graph. Which statement best corrects the student?

options.text: The graphs open in opposite directions, so no comparison is possible
options.misconception: treats opposite openings as blocking a width comparison

options.text: Width depends on the absolute value of a, so |-6| makes it narrower
The negative sign multiplies the width by -6 and widens the graph
options.misconception: extends the sign-as-stretch confusion to the width itself

options.text: The graph of y = x^2 is always wider because 1 is the least coefficient
options.misconception: assumes coefficient 1 produces the widest possible opening

questions.explanation: Width is controlled by |a| alone, and the sign only sets the direction of opening. Since |-6| = 6 is much larger than |1|, the y = -6x^2 graph leaves the x-axis about six times as fast and is therefore narrower, not wider.
questions.hint: Strip away the sign and compare the absolute values.

questions.learningObjective: diagnose a reversed width comparison for a coefficient between zero and one
questions.stem: A worksheet states: 'Because 0.25 is less than 1, the graph of y = 0.25x^2 is narrower than the graph of y = x^2.' Which option identifies the error?

options.text: The error is that y = 0.25x^2 opens downward, so widths cannot match
options.misconception: invents a direction claim the coefficient does not support

options.text: The error is that 0.25 is greater than 1, so the claim reverses
options.misconception: misstates the size of 0.25 while ignoring the width rule

options.text: The error is that width depends on the sign, and both are positive here
options.misconception: confuses the sign rule with the width rule

questions.learningObjective: determine a leading coefficient that matches a given width and opening direction
questions.stem: Two satellite dishes are modeled by y = ax^2 and y = 3x^2. Both dishes open upward and are congruent. Find the value of a.
questions.explanation: Congruent parabolas that open the same way share both the direction and the width, and width is fixed by |a|. Matching the absolute value gives |a| = 3, and the shared upward opening forces a to be positive, so a = 3.
questions.hint: Match the absolute value first, then use the opening direction to fix the sign.

questions.stem: A student plots y = x^2, then y = 3x^2, then y = 9x^2 and reports that the curves get progressively narrower. Which explanation accounts for this?

options.text: Each step raises the vertex, which squeezes the curve inward
options.misconception: attributes width to the height of the vertex

options.text: Each step triples the sign, which stretches the curve toward the x-axis
options.misconception: treats the coefficient as if it changed sign on each step

options.text: Each step triples the absolute value, so y grows faster and the curve pinches in
Each step moves the axis of symmetry, which narrows the curve

questions.learningObjective: explain mechanistically why larger absolute values narrow a graph
questions.stem: A student reads that the larger the absolute value of a, the narrower the graph, and asks why this is true. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: A larger |a| rotates the axis of symmetry toward the x-axis
options.misconception: believes the axis of symmetry tilts when the coefficient grows

options.text: A larger |a| moves the vertex further out, which squeezes the graph inward
options.misconception: believes the vertex moves when only the coefficient changes

options.text: A larger |a| multiplies x^2 more strongly, so y grows faster away from zero
A larger |a| shrinks x itself, so the graph covers less horizontal distance
options.misconception: believes the input values shrink rather than the outputs growing

questions.explanation: For a fixed x the output equals a times x squared, so raising |a| raises the output at every point away from zero. The graph therefore climbs or drops more steeply, and steepness is what pulls the arms in and makes the parabola narrower.

questions.topic: Axis of symmetry from vertex form
questions.learningObjective: read the axis of symmetry from a quadratic in vertex form
questions.practice: reading a graph feature from a rule
questions.stem: A sprinkler throws water along the path modelled by h(x) = -3(x - 4) squared + 5, where x is the horizontal distance in metres. Along which vertical line is the path symmetric?

options.misconception: flips the sign of the value inside the bracket
confuses the constant term with the axis location
names a horizontal line instead of the vertical axis

questions.explanation: In vertex form a(x - h) squared + k the vertex sits at (h, k), and the parabola is symmetric about the vertical line through the vertex. Here h is 4, so the axis is x = 4. The bracket reads x minus 4, so the axis is at positive 4, not negative 4; a learner who reads the minus sign as part of the value lands on option B.
questions.hint: Set the bracket equal to zero.

questions.stem: Two bridges have arch shapes modelled by y = x squared and y = 0.2 x squared, measured in metres. Which statement about their graphs is correct?

options.text: The 0.2 arch is wider because smaller multiplier stretches less per unit of x
The 0.2 arch is narrower because a smaller coefficient grows faster
options.misconception: reverses how the coefficient scales the output

options.text: Both arches have the same width because the squared term dominates
options.misconception: ignores the multiplier entirely

options.text: The 0.2 arch opens downward because its coefficient is a decimal
options.misconception: believes decimals flip the opening direction

questions.explanation: Each unit step in x multiplies by the coefficient before squaring adds the growth, so a smaller positive coefficient produces a smaller output at the same distance from the vertex and therefore a wider arch. Both parabolas open upward because both coefficients are positive. The trap in option B is the intuition that small numbers grow slowly only in the wrong direction: smaller here means flatter, not steeper.

The whole graph shifts 6 units to the left

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Direction of opening
questions.learningObjective: determine whether a quadratic opens upward or downward from its leading coefficient
questions.stem: A water fountain's stream is modelled by y = -0.5 x squared + 3. Which statement describes the shape of the stream's graph?

options.text: It opens downward and has a highest point
It opens upward and has a lowest point
options.misconception: ignores the negative sign on the leading coefficient

options.text: It opens downward and has a lowest point
options.misconception: knows the direction but names the wrong extreme

options.text: It is a straight line because the coefficient is less than one
options.misconception: believes a small coefficient removes the curve

questions.explanation: The sign of the leading coefficient decides the opening: a negative coefficient makes outputs decrease as x moves away from the vertex, so the parabola opens downward. Opening downward means the vertex is a maximum, the highest point on the graph. A learner who remembers only that minus means down may still name a lowest point, which is why option C pairs the right direction with the wrong extreme.
questions.hint: Check whether larger x makes y larger or smaller.
